vocab.definition: a very large molecule made of many small repeating units.
the small molecule that joins to make a polymer.
the part of the polymer that repeats over and over.
attraction between polymer chains — fairly strong.

misconceptions.wrong: Polymers are made of one giant covalent lattice.
misconceptions.right: They are long molecules held to each other by intermolecular forces.

misconceptions.wrong: Polymers are gases at room temperature.
misconceptions.right: Forces between long chains make them solids.

misconceptions.wrong: Monomer and polymer are the same thing.
misconceptions.right: Monomers join to build the polymer.

infoPanels.title: MONOMER → POLYMER
workedSteps: Many small monomers (e.g. ethene) react together.
Monomers join into one long chain.
The repeat unit is shown in brackets with n.

questions.text: State what is meant by a polymer. [1 mark]
Name the monomer used to make poly(ethene). [1 mark]
Explain why polymers are solid at room temperature. [2 marks]
Draw the repeat unit for poly(ethene). [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Many small ______ join together, as the ______ bond opens, to form a polymer.

questions.text: Suggest why polymers do not conduct electricity. [1 mark]

footer.tip: A polymer is one long molecule; the repeat unit is written in brackets with 'n'.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why are the forces between polymer chains stronger than between small molecules?
